title: Wesley So, Rachael Li Lead By Full Point Ahead Of Final Round
summary: It's the GM Wesley So show at the 2026 U.S. Chess Championship as the three-time winner coasts to the final round with a full-point lead on GMs Fabiano Caruana and Grigoriy Oparin. He made a quick draw with GM Hans Niemann to maintain that lead, but there were two decisive games in this section. GM Sam Shankland won a sharp game against GM Sam Sevian in the Sicilian Najdorf Poisoned Pawn Variation, while GM Levon Aronian worked his magic to beat GM Ray Robson in a queen endgame. Rookie WIM Rachael Li is in the home stretch of the 2026 U.S. Women's Chess Championship with a full-point lead on just one player, IM Alice Lee. There were five decisive games out of six, with wins scored by Li, Lee (a must-win to stay in the race), IM Tatev Abrahamyan, IM Carissa Yip, and IM Anna Sargsyan against IM Rose Atwell, WGM Thalia Cervantes, IM Anna Zatonskih, IM Nazi Paikidze, and WGM Jennifer Yu, respectively. The one draw was in FM Megan Paragua vs. GM Irina Krush. The 11th and final round is on Wednesday, October 21, starting at 1 p.m. ET / 19:00 CEST / 10:30 p.m. IST. Standings After Round 10: Open Standings After Round 10: Women Round 10 Results: Open There were several dramatic games and two decisive ones, but nothing changed the prevailing fact that So is one round away from earning his fourth national title in the U.S. Along with the prestige, it comes with a $55,000 payday (not including the Winner's Bonus of $7,000 or the Finish Strong Prize of $5,000). No player will earn the Fischer Bonus Prize, for which one must win a minimum of five consecutive games to be eligible. It was a quick day at the office for Grandmaster So, who finished his game with Niemann in less than an hour. A theoretical line of the Nimzo-Indian Defense quickly went into an endgame with mass trades. The strategy in the final stretch, in his words, is "to remove games from the tournament." So shared mixed praise for his opponent on the broadcast after the game. "Hans is a really good player. I actually had high hopes for him for his first Olympiad this year, but it didn't work out well. I'm not sure what's going on with his classical chess career." So said that a few months ago, Niemann looked to be competing at the level of GMs Javokhir Sindarov and Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu. "Because he said he's going to be the classical world champion, I'm not sure when he's planning on this dream. Because he told me a couple of days ago that he's focused on other chess formats, not classical," So added. A draw is a good result in the next round, but So said he would also like to win. He noticed that he's briefly higher than GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov, who lost in round two of the European Club Cup 2026, and that he, So, was back in the top-five. He'd like to keep it that way. As for the three other draws, the most consequential were GM Jeffery Xiong vs. Caruana and Oparin vs. GM Abhimanyu Mishra, as a win in either game could have put Caruana or Oparin a half-point behind the leader. Caruana even played the Scandinavian Defense as an attempt to win with Black, but his opponent played a perfect game. Both boards exhibited 99 accuracy by all four players. "Nobody checks the Scandinavian anymore. It's not so bad!" Sounds like a ringing endorsement from Fabiano Caruana! https://t.co/2LvzOQg8dc There was also a draw between GMs Awonder Liang and Andy Woodward, leaving both players on 5.5 points—a good score, but not enough to win the tournament. As for the two decisive games, the battle of Sams was the most exciting as Sevian rejuvenated the highly theoretical and relatively rarely seen Poisoned Pawn Variation of the Najdorf Sicilian. Shankland wasn't expecting a Najdorf at all and said, "I think he got a little too ambitious at some point.... This was certainly not a glorious win for me, but after everything I've been through this tournament I'll take it." This was certainly not a glorious win for me, but after everything I've been through this tournament I'll take it. —Sam Shankland It was a full-on slugfest, with both players finding game-winning and game-saving resources as well as committing game-losing mistakes. Indeed, when Sevian had a relatively "risk-free" advantage in the end, he made the last blunder, the unfortunate and irreversible 35...Qg1??. It's a game full of twists and turns, and GM Rafael Leitao takes us through the Game of the Day below.

title: Abdusattorov, Giri, Erdogmus All Beaten In European Club Cup Round 4
summary: GMs Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Anish Giri, and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus all lost in round four of the 2026 European Chess Club Cup, falling to GMs Aydin Suleymanli, Pranav Venkatesh, and Karthikeyan Murali respectively. While Abdusattorov was rescued by his SuperChess Romania teammates for a 4-2 victory, top-seed Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club could only scrape a 3-3 draw after the losses for Giri and Erdogmus. Meanwhile, CE Gambit Bonnevoie has taken the sole lead in the 2026 European Women's Chess Club Cup after defeating top seed Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo. GM Elina Danielian's fourth win in a row, against IM Stavroula Tsolakidou, was enough to clinch the match 2.5-1.5 after GM Koneru Humpy let a winning position slip against IM Klaudia Kulon. Round five is on Wednesday, October 21, starting at 8 a.m. ET / 14:00 CEST / 5:30 p.m. IST. None of the matches at the top were easy in round four, with Giri and Erdogmus' Turkish team held to a draw by sixth-seed Elektroprivreda. Other notable results included 11th-seed Aix-en-Provence tying fifth-seed Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai in a match where all games were decisive and GM Marc'Andria Maurizzi beat GM Pranesh M on top board. We're down to just four teams on a perfect score, with the surprise package the 12th-seeded SK K CERO INVEST Nitra. In round four the team overcame 10th-seed Beer Sheva Chess Club, with GM Vasyl Ivanchuk beating GM Victor Mikhalevski on top board. Open Standings After Round 4 (Top 10)

title: GothamChess Returns To NYT Bestseller List, Holds Amazon’s Top 2 Chess Spots
summary: IM Levy Rozman has another New York Times bestseller. His new book, How to Win at Chess, Next Level, has reached the prestigious list, while his two How to Win at Chess titles currently rank in the top two spots on Amazon’s bestselling chess books chart. His publishing debut, How to Win at Chess: The Ultimate Guide for Beginners and Beyond, topped several Amazon lists and ranked fourth on the New York Times Advice, How-To & Miscellaneous list shortly after its October 2023 release. Three years later, the original book continues to attract readers alongside its follow-up, with the two books now holding the number-one and number-two positions on Amazon’s Best Sellers in Chess list. He celebrated the milestone on his X account. Back to back NYT Bestseller. Thank you all ❤️ https://t.co/gvAeNuV9wN Released on October 6, How to Win at Chess, Next Level: The Ultimate Guide for Intermediate Play follows March’s "chew-proof" chess book for babies. This time, Rozman targets readers ready to move beyond the basics, with the publisher identifying its intended audience as players rated around 1000–1600. In an interview with Federico Marin in El Mundo, he explained that writing books has been about more than adding another revenue stream to his successful career as the world’s biggest chess YouTuber with more than eight million subscribers. “It’s not about the money at all. I wrote the first book because I wanted to change the way people learn. A book is very different from a video. I wanted to leave a legacy.” I wrote the first book because I wanted to change the way people learn. A book is very different from a video. I wanted to leave a legacy.—Levy Rozman The permanence of a printed book holds particular appeal for someone whose audience largely comes from an online platform. “YouTube, with its algorithms, could decide tomorrow not to recommend me anymore. A book is always there, and I wanted to write a very modern one, with things that no one else had done,” Rozman told Marin. Writing for an audience that already understands the basics presented a different challenge from introducing newcomers to the game. "I felt more pressure. It’s easier to write for people who don’t know," he said. "I had to think a lot about why a player reaches, say, 1500 or 1600 Elo points on Chess.com." I had to think a lot about why a player reaches, say, 1500 or 1600 Elo points on Chess.com.—Levy Rozman Finding suitable examples meant looking closely at how players at that level actually play. "I researched, reviewed games, analyzed hundreds of thousands of them, and I think I found some very good examples." The follow-up comes after more than 300,000 copies of his first book have been printed, making it one of the most popular chess books ever. It has also been translated into around 20 languages, making it truly global. Rozman had already expressed his surprise at that international reach when speaking to Chess.com in March. "It definitely exceeded my wildest expectations," he told FM Mike Klein. "It’s incredible. When I visit European countries, people bring me the book in their language, which is insane." Rozman will soon be meeting more fans in person. His second European tour begins in Cologne on October 25, with further stops in Munich, Breda, Amsterdam, and Zurich before concluding in London on November 10. The shows will feature live Guess the Elo segments, games against fans, and chess lessons.

title: Nakamura Starts 7/7, Wins Titled Tuesday
summary: GM Hikaru Nakamura won a dramatic Titled Tuesday on October 20, taking down GM Alireza Firouzja in the final round to win the event with 9.5/11. Nakamura also needed tiebreaks to beat out GMs Dmitry Andreikin and Sina Movahed, who finished in second and third, respectively, also on 9.5 points. Nakamura extended his lead in the 2026-27 CCT Standings with the victory, his first in Titled Tuesday since May. In case you missed it, here's this week's broadcast with GM David Howell filling in for GM Robert Hess: Nakamura was also the last player on 100 percent, starting 7/7. If his seventh-round game to get there against GM Liem Le seemed familiar, that might be because they followed Nakamura's seventh-round game against GM Alexey Sarana from two weeks ago. Like Sarana, Le missed a drawing subtlety on move 16 of the opening, and Nakamura went on to win.

title: Where chess meets its fans: Join side activities of the Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match
summary: The Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026, taking place in Geneva from 22 November to 12 December, is the most important chess event of the year. Reigning World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju and challenger Javokhir Sindarov will battle for the crown and the title of World Champion. But this three-week event is about more than the very pinnacle of professional chess. It is also a celebration of the game itself, bringing together players, fans, and future champions. Every recent World Championship has featured a rich programme of side events, and Geneva will be no exception. If you’re coming to Geneva to follow the match, be sure to reserve your place at one of the many activities on offer. The Salesforce FIDE World Championship match is a magnet for grandmasters, and several elite players, including former world champions, will be meeting and interacting with spectators throughout the event. After all, where else can you play against the great Viswanathan Anand or meet one of the biggest inspirations in women’s chess, Alexandra Kosteniuk? The programme begins on 24 November, when Anand shares memories and insights from his own World Championship journeys. You may already know some of the stories from his bestselling memoir Master Mind, but this is a chance to hear first-hand from one of the legends of the game. Swiss stars Alexandra Kosteniuk, the 12th Women’s World Champion, and Grandmaster Yannick Pelletier will lead a variety of activities throughout the event. Highlights include Pelletier’s fan blitz session during Game 3 and Kosteniuk’s audience challenge during Game 1. During Game 4, Grandmaster Anna Muzychuk, one of the few women ever to surpass the 2600 rating mark, will team up with fan favourite Anish Giri for a tandem simultaneous exhibition. Both will also take part in additional events and activities on other days during the championship. Be sure to bookmark the side events calendar so you don’t miss any new additions. Many activities require advance registration, so secure your place early before the spots are gone! You can find all the information and registration details at: https://tickets.fide.com/en/events
